en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jianguan:
The transmission of Caoxi spread throughout the world like the offspring of a horse; none was more flourishing than during the Li Tang (Tang) dynasty. This master was a treasure of Shu.
Subsequently, Deshan and Guifeng first appeared. By the time of our dynasty’s revival, Yuanwu was particularly prominent;
since then, there have been elders such as Chijue and Wuzhun who have served across the Five Mountains, all of whom were preeminent in their time.
Although I have heard their teachings, I did not have the opportunity to know them personally. In the year Yichu (1265),...

Passing through Jian Pass to enter Min, he came to Yurong. We sought each other out by the stream. Although my friends beyond the secular world are many, it was from this point that I first came to know a man from Shu.
Observing his countenance, it was stately and imposing; listening to his speech, it was clear and flowing.
His understanding was thorough and his insight penetrating—this was the learning of the Southern School. Yet his spirit was bold, distinctive, and lofty—this was the air of the Western Capital.
We conversed back and forth for some time; if he had any intention toward me, his heart was truly moved by it. I always regretted that he departed so hurriedly.
Before long, I heard that he had already passed away, and I lamented this for many days.

Three autumns have since passed like the turning of an arm, yet I did not know that this record had already been published at Yishan. In the autumn of the Gengwu year, my elder brother Ze sent it to me; although...

The three handles of the ladles are all present; their edges are sharp and steep, frosty and piercingly cold. Killing and giving life proceed with total freedom, beyond any attempt at grasping or measurement.
He is truly a seedling of Fengxue and Yangqi; I only regret that I have not yet met him in person within his chamber to encounter his dynamic conditions.
The chanting of these verses of praise should not end here. Could it be that the transmitters omitted parts and failed to include them?

Or did this old man cast them aside and refuse to preserve them? Therefore, I offer these disordered words in its stead: Zen is fundamentally without awakening; yet without awakening, there would be no insight.
The Way is fundamentally without words; yet without words, there would be no transmission. Since awakening arises through words, the transmission of this compilation is sufficient. If...
To speak while turning one's back on awakening and remaining deluded—whether calling something sweet or bitter—is in every case a poisonous drug. Though much of it may be produced, what use is it?
Jian Guan, whose secular name was Ziyi, was a native of Jianzhou and a Dharma heir of Chongze. He currently presides over Qingcheng in his hometown.
On the Double Ninth day of the Gengwu year of the Xianchun era, [this was written by] Zhongdafu, newly appointed Bige Xiuzhuan, and Acting Commissioner of Jianning Prefecture.
Written by Lin Xiyi of Chongyou Guan at Mount Wuyi:
My Dharma Brother of Jian Pass tucked away a dagger in his sleeve, yet did not stand alone in peril; those with iron visages and copper heads begged for their lives upon seeing him from afar.
Although he has now passed away, his sharp blade remains as cold as frost. Those who lick the honey should each take care. From Chun, sent southward;
a hand-written letter with one prostration from his younger brother, Xuefeng Weiyi.

Attendants: Shan-gong and De-xiu, compilers.
In the first month of the third year of the Jiaxi era, the Master entered the monastery.
Pointing to the triple gate, he said: "This one gate of mine has never had a bolt or latch; it is half-closed and half-open, with its eastern leaf and western leaf."
However, a thousand hearings are not equal to one seeing.
Occupying the abbot’s quarters, he neither utters shouts nor wields the staff; such a monk who carries his own life does not fish for those who come of their own accord.
The Preface to the Mountain Gate: Not a single character bears a stroke; eight words contain no duplicity. The literary brilliance is perfectly clear—what need is there for further prolixity?
A Brief Account of the Rivers and Lakes. Where the journey cannot reach, take one step; where speech cannot arrive, utter a single word.
The masters of Jing Mountain acted with valorous resolve; the venerable master of Lingyin drew his sword to assist him.
But tell me, where does the crux lie? Listen with your own eyes.
[The Master] held up the Dharma robe and said: "At Huangmei at midnight; before Mount Jijue. Receiving the void and connecting with echoes;
they have deceived one another. Layman Yi, I am now deceiving all of you. He then donned the robe.
The Essential Outline: At Fuhuyan, the heights give rise to winds across ten thousand ravines; at Qinglong, the waters are swift, with waves surging a thousand fathoms.
The gateway of the ancient Buddhas stands wide open, and the primary truth is proclaimed with blazing intensity. Here, you new elder—arriving at this place—[must act].
The entire body is mouth; the entire body is tongue. What more could possibly be said? I can do no more than take this established case as it is and present it to you all.
Those who are quick-witted enough to take it up will find that the three directions are at once hushed and tranquil.

The four seas are peaceful and clear; the rains fall in clumps and the winds blow in gentle strands. The people are healthy and the things of the world are abundant. At such a time as this, what is it like? It is said:

"When the Way is prosperous, the Emperor’s edict is not transmitted; when the times are clear, do not sing the song of Great Peace. Changsha Jingcen raised the words of the Three Sages: "Whenever I meet a person, I come forth;
yet when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others. Xinghua said: "Whenever I meet a person, I do not come forth; yet when I do come forth, I immediately act for them."
The Master held up [the staff] and said: "Great assembly, do you know where these two great elders fell? Subduing the enemy with golden drums falling from heaven;
Han Xin’s spear and banner arrayed against the water."
That evening’s informal discourse (the questions and answers are not recorded). A long sword leaning against the heavens; its edge is not revealed. The Three Sages cannot discern it;
how could the Ten Saints know it? (He raises his staff and says: Look, look! The edge is revealed! Its cold light pierces the Dipper;

its vigorous spirit overcomes the frost. Meeting a Buddha, he kills the Buddha; meeting an Ancestor, he kills the Ancestor. Among all the people in the entire world, who dares to look directly at it with their true eye?
"Is there anyone here who disregards their own peril and death, capable of turning back from under the blade? (He strikes the staff.
"I grant you one point. He then raised another case: Master Mada ordered a monk to deliver a letter to National Preceptor Guoyi at Mount Jing.
Upon opening the seal once, he saw a circular mark. He then applied a single dot within the circle and sent it back.
When National Teacher Zhong heard of this, he said, "Master Qin was still deluded by Master Ma. [The Commentator] remarks:
Master Ma exhausted all his lifelong skills, yet before Guoyi’s face, they were not worth a single dot. Why, then, did Nanyang say, "Qin..."?
The Master was still deluded by Master Ma. (After a long silence, he said: "A person must first insult themselves;
a state must first attack itself. He ascended the hall. The first phrase is a teaching of the highest capacity. Gautama did not understand it; Bodhidharma did not know it. Whether you know it or not:
after the rain, a thousand peaks are verdant; with spring waters, a single stream is full.
The two *vīnaras*, Guan and Jing, went up to the hall. With a single blow of the mallet, they were right there—obscure and bewildered.
Without even a single blow, it was utterly groundless. After all, how is it? Seek the work amidst busyness; observe the message within stillness. Even amidst clamor, seek the news in tranquility.
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: The moon is full in the heavens; it is half-full among men. Even for an enlightened monk, seeing is like not seeing.
Do you see? (He hurls down his whisk. "The cup falls to the ground; the plate shatters into seven pieces. Ascending the hall:
The single path that leads upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages. Before you have even raised a thought, you are already separated from it by the great trichiliocosm. Therefore:
Xuefeng rolls the ball; Heshan beats the drum; Yangshan plants his spade; Dizang tills the fields.
Although this is so, how can a short rope draw from a deep spring?
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: On this very day last year, I met the winter solstice; frost and snow struck my head and face.

This year’s winter solstice has arrived once more; plum blossoms at the corner of the roof play in the morning clarity. (Patting his knee) I laugh at the *Spring and Autumn Annals* for its vain recording of clouds.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "It is so cold! Where can one avoid it? Upon jagged ice, amidst deep snow—there is a reason for this, yet no handle to grasp.
Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, and the temple steward’s eyebrows and beard fell off."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] held up his whisk and said: "Taken up at random by the hand, it hits the mark every time one tries.
Light as a goose feather, yet heavy as a mountain. [He threw down the whisk and said: "Though it is but a dead snake, it must still be handled with life.
Ascending the hall: Four times nine is thirty-six; sleeping at night is like staying out in the open. In the silver sea, eyes dazzle and flowers bloom; in the jade towers, the cold is biting.
He rose from his seat. [The Master] said, "I bring up the story of the Second Patriarch standing in the snow until it reached his waist, all for nothing.
A flawless piece of jade was buried alive. Entering the hall: Yesterday it rained; today it is sunny. The peach blossoms open their mouths and laugh; nowhere can one find Lingyun.
Is there anyone here today who has 'caught the fish without casting the line'? (After a long silence, he said: "To conceal one's brilliance is to kill the man."
The Buddha ascends the hall on his birthday: Two thousand years ago, his entire body was covered in filth; two thousand years later, his face is covered in dust.
Even if one were to wash with the waters of the winding Yellow River until the year of the donkey, it would still not be clean.
The Head Seat and the Librarian, Xie, take up the whisk and ascend the hall. With a reputation as vast as the heavens, he is the Muzhou who bites with urgent ferocity—a tiger that dozes.
Where one cannot go, he takes a step; where one cannot speak, he utters a word.

Deshan and Linji have eyes like rheumy, blinking lids; their staffs and shouts fly back and forth, leaving no room for maneuver. Xinghua could not restrain his impatience. (He strikes the meditation staff.)
Following the pattern, amidst the brilliant sunlight, white rain falls. (Suddenly calling to the assembly: "Take care not to get the corners of your *kāṣāya* robes wet.
Enters the hall. Worldly affairs are wearying; they are not as good as dwelling on a mountain ridge.

Lying beneath the wisteria vines, with a block of stone for a pillow—this is why Xu You washed his ears and Chao Fu fed his oxen. Furthermore, what do others say? Why not eat their dregs and drink their broth?
Diluted. Following the waves and mixing with the current—this crew of board-carrying fellows can grasp but cannot let go;
they can let go but cannot grasp. But what is the phrase for total grasping and total letting go?
(Striking the meditation seat with his whisk) The Great Peng spreads its wings, covering the ten continents; the swallows by the hedge chirp in vain.
Ascending the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival, [the Master] raised his whisk and called to the assembly, saying: "Do you see it? It cannot be named; it cannot be described.
It is the method for shedding the old form and changing the bones, the secret instruction for raising the dead and returning life.
For those who can believe in it, a single dose is enough to instantly eliminate all ailments and bring about total peace and well-being. Why must Sudhana go so far as to gather medicine anew?"
At Zhongxia, he ascended the hall: "Day after day, in the blink of an eye, midsummer passes. Old Xinghua was ignorant; he added a handle to his almsbowl.
This drew in seekers of the profound from the four seas, gathering in groups of three or two to deliberate over this talk.
A-he-he! Selling pine-wind in the sixth month—fear it has no price in the human world."
Please attend the assembly for the formal instruction. If you wish to clarify this Way, you must encounter the right person. Once the right person is encountered, the harvest is tenfold.
Now tell me, what is this word "Way"? (After a long silence, he said: To explain it through intellectual penetration is unfitting. Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth:
Autumn has not yet frosted, yet the chrysanthemums are in full bloom. Thousands upon thousands of blossoms emit their fragrance from their calyxes; three branches, two...

The golden branches are yellow as if withered; this is neither for worldly dissemination nor for Buddhist deliberation. On the ninth day of the ninth month, the Double Ninth Festival, he ascended the hall and said:
"It is strange how deep the night is cold, and how heavy the clear frost is at dawn. The waters of the twin ravines are silent; the clouds over the thousand peaks—"
Desire freezes. Here it is cold and still; there it is hot and bustling. One does not know which has gained the advantage.
How shameful, Old Yangqi, you frozen scum!
Xie, the Head Seat of the West Hall and the Librarian, ascends the hall. (Holding up his whisk, he says: "To uphold the teaching beyond the categories, the constellations shift and the stars turn.
Zizang does not understand; Brother Hai does not know. It is intolerable that Muzhou, a fellow carrying a single wooden board, ruins the little sick child of Linji.
(He slaps the meditation seat and says: "To whom is this clear meaning being spoken?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "At the moment of seeing the seeing—*kāti kāti*. That which sees is not the seeing—*prākāti*.
Even seeing is already apart from seeing—*prasaṅkāti*. Seeing is such that nothing can reach it—*bodhi svāhā*. (He suddenly called out to the assembly:
"Do you see the Old Man Śākyamuni? (He then descended from his seat.)
Ascending the hall: The heavens are cold and the earth is freezing; days are short and nights are long. The dead ashes have been stirred through until nothing remains to be discussed.
Last night at the third watch, the moon shone upon the window.

Ascending the hall: Acting with nothing to do, performing with nothing to achieve; with head and face covered in dust and ash, trailing water and mud—those who wish to see Xinghua in such a state must quickly take care of his two eyebrows.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Tathāgata-dhyāna resides right at the edge of the lips; the meaning of the Patriarchs does not exceed the span of a square inch.
Why is it that ten out of five pairs know as if they did not know, and see as if they did not see? (After a long silence, he said: It is simply because it is too close to the Sacred Festival.
Ascending the hall, the True Dharma Wheel is lightly turned. The sun rises in the midst of the heavens; the clouds part from the face of the mountain. Like a *utpala*...
The *tán-huá* (dharma-flower) appears but once in an age.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "There is one person standing atop a hundred-foot pole, striding with wide steps, yet unable to speak.
There is another person in the midst of a crowd of ten thousand people, reviling the rain and scolding the wind, yet unable to walk. Now tell me, which of these two is superior?"
[The Master] says: "Dividing the bath for the Buddha, we ascend the hall.
When the Buddha’s body is three feet tall, the handle of the ladle is three feet long; when the Buddha’s body is one zhang six chi tall, the handle of the ladle is one zhang six chi long;
when the Buddha’s body is immeasurable hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions, billions, nayutas of yojanas tall, [the handle of the ladle is likewise immeasurable]. This—
The handle of the ladle is likewise so. The Blue Dragon brings the base to repay deep kindness; following custom, fragrant water is poured upon the fontanelle.
Regarding the "Former Resident" ascending to the Hall: Xuan Sha did not cross the ridge; the root of the staff has taken birth, there is no need to prune it.
Baoshou did not cross the river; the bowl lacks a handle, there is no need to attach one. It is just like the youth Sudhana at the eastern outskirts of the city of Awakening.
Having received the instructions of Mañjuśrī, he traveled through one hundred and ten cities and attended fifty-three spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
At the very end, within the sound of a finger-snap in Maitreya’s pavilion—was there still this news or not? (He then said:
*Suru suru*.
Ascending the hall on the full moon of the sixth month: The scorching heat blazes fiercely; where can one find refuge? Not within the boiling cauldrons or the glowing embers.
Upon the northern window, after a nap of deep, sweet slumber, One listens closely to the pines’ breeze mingling with the flowing stream.
The Chief Seat and Librarian Xie took up the whisk and ascended the hall for the discourse: "To see at the very first glance is to see all; heaven turns and earth revolves.

When the principle of the school is penetrated and the teaching is mastered, the wind calls the tiger and the clouds gather for the dragon. But tell me, when Baizhang was struck by Mazu’s single shout, why did he remain deaf for three days?"
(After a long silence, he said: "The customs of Min and Shu are the same. Entering the hall, [he said:
"The sun may grow cold, and the moon may grow hot; no demons can destroy the True Teaching. But what, pray tell, is the True Teaching?
The spring water dripping from the eaves never ceases; the cry of the autumn insects beneath the steps is even more piercing."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Day after day, autumn after autumn. Counting from the beginning on one's fingers, and counting from the beginning again.
When will the flight of the crow and the running of the hare ever cease? (He calls to the assembly: Is there anyone here who does not follow the fluctuations of worldly fortune?
(He strikes the meditation seat and descends.)
Ascending the hall at Xiuxiao Bridge: gaining the path, block the path; crossing the bridge, break the bridge. Not constrained by the two banks, not lingering in the midstream.
Even if you can understand walking while riding a water buffalo, I shall ask you further: why, empty-handed, do you grasp a hoe?
Ascending the hall: Before winter and after winter, sand flies and stones run. When the season arrives, there is no room for hands in one’s sleeves.
Although Xinghua lacks the stratagem of driving the wind and racing the lightning, he must still respond to this moment. (He strikes the sounding staff and says:
"One nine, two nines."

Xie Weina, the Guest Master and Vice Abbot, ascends the hall. Once the ten strikes of the mallet have settled the fundamental principles, the matters of sending off and welcoming are one and the same.
With a hundred verticals and a thousand horizontals, there is penetration and transformation: a handleless colander scoops up the spring breeze.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The sharpness of Prajñā, the blazing flame of the Vajra—confronted directly, it strikes home; so sudden, it is difficult to discern. (He held up his whisk and said: "Do you see?
A gust of spring wind arrives, and fallen petals fly in pieces."
Head Seat Huanglong Ning ascends the hall: "In the past, when at Yujia, the division of spoils did not accord with the fire.
Today we meet unexpectedly; as before, the assembly acts thus—or does it not? Muzhou’s carrying-board, Yunmen’s lame leg."
Recorded at the Yunyan Shouning Chan Monastery in Longxing Prefecture.
Compiled by Attendant Hui Cheng and Rui Zhang. Ascending the Hall for the Imperial Birthday:
"The mind is like empty space, immeasurable; The lifespan of the Sage Ruler is likewise so. (He struck the sounding block.)
The Abbot, having thus used this Dharma to repay the Imperial Grace, ascends the hall to declare that there is nothing superior to this between heaven and earth.
One summer consists of ninety days; half a month has already passed. Someone asks about the "candle-man" and the "ice": the nostrils remain as they were.
(He then extends his hands and says: "How does my hand compare to the Buddha’s hand?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "This phrase is to be struck down; that phrase is also to be struck down. Deshan burned his commentaries and notes; Linji burned his meditation board.
How pitiable, how laughable—a pair of unperforated iron hammers! When will you ever dream of the True Dharma Eye?"
Ascending the hall: The mind of the ancient Buddhas is right here now. The spring breeze sweeps vast and wide; the spring rain falls in torrents. (Striking the meditation seat, he says:
On the lofty mountains and flowing waters, few are those who understand the music.
The Buddha ascends the hall for the discourse on his *nirvāṇa*: "The Dharma-body fills the vast void; its appearing and disappearing have never had a fixed trace.
Only Pāpīyān is permitted to know this meaning; half-stealing joy, half-beating his breast."
Ascending the hall: The season having arrived, its principle is naturally manifest. Row upon row, the rice seedlings float in green; village after village, the wheat plays in yellow.
Half a window of mountain moon is white; one pillow of bamboo wind is cool. Laughing until he falls over is Old Deng of the mountainside.
Xie, the Abbot, and Weina, the Attendant, ascended the hall. Advancing with propriety and withdrawing with propriety, I have recorded this one discourse;
it does not reside within paper or cloth. Thus, Zizang was smeared by Master Ma, and Kebin suffered the neglect of Xinghua.
For a thousand ages to come, these shall remain on people’s lips and teeth. The kindness is too great to repay; the pain penetrates to the very marrow of the bones. Let us examine this.
Come! Xuan Sha has reached the bottom.
Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: within the ocean of enlightened nature, all is perfectly integrated. When heard, there is wealth and honor; once seen, one is poor.
"When one reaches an impasse, there must be change; through change, there comes penetration. (He throws down his staff. "The straw sandals are as fierce as tigers; the staff is as alive as a dragon.
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: Before the fifteenth day, it is as clear as a mirror; after the fifteenth day, it is as curved as a sickle.
It is precisely the fifteenth day. (Pressing his knees with both hands, he says: No one understands this meaning; it causes me to remember Nanquan.
On the Double Ninth, he ascends the hall: The autumn river is clear, the autumn moon is white. Climbing high, both eyes are empty; walking alone, heaven and earth seem narrow.
A single hand has never been raised; yellow chrysanthemums already fill the palm. From the beginning, good fortune has fled to the cramped home of the petty scholar;
for my part, there is but a cup of *zhuyou* tea.
After the formal practice, one ascends the hall; at the head of the latrine, atop the dung pit, the stench permeates the heavens—how can one draw near? One.
To one who has already relieved himself, I give a sharp prick with a needle. To one who is vividly and clearly manifest—why is it thirty feet?
Reward those who have merit. Entering the hall:
"The constant light manifests before us; it stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. (With the whisk, he makes a single stroke. Here, I make this one stroke.
Severed. There is another shortcut. Why does a man with clear eyes fall into a well?
Having traveled to the Jewel Mountain to behold the *śarīra* of the Buddha’s crown and visited the nine lotuses of Tuṣita, he returns. He ascends the hall and says:

"I have come directly from the Jewel Mountain, having gathered the treasures of the Jewel Mountain. (Holding up his whisk, he says: "A single piece of jade, flawless; a thousand peaks, the clouds remove their hats."
"Hidden nowhere by the side of Mount Jiulian; difficult to find even within the Tuṣita Palace.
Return and beat the drum for all to come and see. (He throws down his whisk. "The jade disk rolls the pearl, and the pearl rolls the disk.

On the occasion of the Winter Solstice, he ascends the hall. (Holding up the staff, he says: "When the six yin months have reached their end, the hordes of demons naturally perish. When the one yang returns, I..."

The Way is greatly flourishing. When the master’s staff stands upright, the worlds of the ten directions stand upright at once; when the master’s staff lies horizontal, the worlds of the ten directions lie horizontal at once.
(He strikes the floor once and says: "The soldiers follow the seal’s turn; the generals march according to the talisman.

When the Buddha ascended the hall, before he had entered the mountains, his spirit pierced the ox and the dipper constellations; having emerged from the mountains, his robes were worn through and exposed.
Elbows! To further say that one saw the morning star at midnight—how thick is that face?
Because of the snow, he ascends the hall: six-flakes of flowers fly; there is no place to plant a锥 (a small awl); ditches are filled and ravines are blocked; every hair and every speck is gone.
"Ha! Suddenly startled, the green mountains are all swept away; again with joy, one carries the spring colors back home.
Entering the hall, he said: "It is most profound and most wondrous; it is most abstruse and most subtle. It cannot be known through consciousness, nor can it be understood through intellect."
If you understand it in this way, you are obstructed by a tangled thicket. If you do not understand it in this way, Fenglin says "Tsha!

Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day, he held up his staff and said: "The root of the staff grows beyond the kalpas; a brand new spring has arrived. I pick it up and show it to all people. (He drew a line with the staff and said:
"I cleave open the thousand peaks of Mount Hua, revealing their exquisite beauty; I release the single current of the Yellow River, letting its clarity flow forth."
Record of the Sayings of Master Xichan Yishan Changqing Chan Temple of Fuzhou, compiled by Attendant Shinēng and Huigōng.
In the fifth month of the first year of the Xiánchūn era, the Master entered the temple. He ascended the seat and offered incense, making the following vow:

"Saintly, it is finished. (The questions and answers are not recorded. He then said: "The First Principle of the Noble Truths is so lofty it cannot be looked up to; it is so deep it cannot be fathomed.

The mind of supreme, wondrous enlightenment is vast enough to encompass heaven and earth, yet subtle enough to enter the Avīci Hell. All Buddhas have personally realized it, yet there is nothing to be attained.
The common people use it daily, yet they do not know it. Where the golden cock crows, all is revealed in its majesty; when the blue phoenix dances..."
Vividly clear! If you can take up this burden here, the assembly on Vulture Peak is entirely present before you.
You may thereby repay the unrequitable debt of gratitude and assist in the transformation of non-action. Do you understand this fully? In the heavens, all stars bow toward the North;
among men, no water flows except toward the East. [The Emperor] cites Emperor Xiaozong’s question to Chan Master Fozhao: "The world..."
"What was accomplished by Your Majesty during the six years at Mount Heng? The Buddha-illuminating [official] replied: "I thought Your Majesty had forgotten.
Today, this humble monk borrows water to offer flowers and has hastily composed a verse: 'The question was clear; the answer was intimate.'"
The Sovereign of Great Peace and his Ministers of Great Peace casually blow away the snow from a thousand peaks; here on this earth and in the Western Heaven, it is spring in one and the same way.

He leaves the two classes of attendants behind as they enter the hall for the current, ready-made public case, which is utterly free of change or transition. Having entered the gate, upon seeing him once—
Behold! When he looks to the left, the lions let out their roars; when he glances to the right, the elephant kings turn back.
The assembly on Vulture Peak remains as it was, gathered together like a single expanse of spring breeze.
Ascending the hall: Of the ninety-day period, two-thirds have passed. The waves of awakening are stilled; the iron boat has no bottom.
As for Hanshan’s water-buffalo—how is it? One must by all means not say: "Everyone is here."
Ascending the hall: The oppressive heat has not yet subsided, and the golden wind is gradually arising. Within the snap of a finger, the gates of the pavilions open.
Do you all see Maitreya? (He then lowers one foot. Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth:
The chrysanthemums are yellow; the *zhuyu* is fragrant. As the season arrives, its principle naturally manifests. Now, for instance:

What is this principle of self-manifestation? Deshan lowered his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters; Ehu entered the monks’ hall with a sudden stride. When Master Jichun of Huangbo arrived, he ascended the hall.
"When masters meet, even 'cracking the egg' and 'pecking the shell' are still off the mark. When realized ones encounter one another, they grasp the whip and turn their heads back.
To examine this from the start, it has already fallen into the secondary. But tell me, what about Yishan today?
"Pebasan, how do you see it? (He snaps his fingers.

"On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascended the hall. For six years he practiced in the Snowy Mountains; it was nearly too much to bear. At midnight, beholding the morning star, he became blind and dazed.
Furthermore, he said: 'How marvelous! All sentient beings throughout the great earth possess the wisdom of the Tathāgata.'"

The marks of virtue can only be realized by abandoning deluded thoughts and attachments; otherwise, they cannot be attained. According to the school of the patch-robed monks (śramaṇas), these are nothing more than stinking leather sandals.
When Chief Seat Xuegu’an held the whisk and ascended the hall, he said: "Speaking is not it; silence is not it; neither speaking nor silence is also not it."
No. Vū’ān has a turning phrase that, in its application, is utterly devoid of even a hair’s breadth of artifice.
